Missing bearer identity, missing tenant identity, payload tenant mismatch, cross-tenant incident correlation, and foreign-tenant legacy fallback all fail closed.
Incident-triggered evaluation preserves tenant_id, incident_id, source_event_id, binding and runtime identity, telemetry event IDs, and trigger reason.
Scheduler retries preserve tick_id and window_id, and completed receipts expose measured duration, SLA, and terminal status.
After lease expiry and successor acquisition, stale save and release attempts cannot alter the successor token or checkpoint, including reuse of the same worker ID.
Timeout retry preserves the logical window; expired and failed claims recover; pending and dead-letter delivery state survives worker replacement without duplicate incident side effects.
Reconciliation remains advisory and cannot mutate runtime, emergency-control, broker, or capital state.
A stale lease token cannot complete or release recovered work; failed delivery remains visible for bounded retry or explicit dead-letter replay.
